Bilateral configuration

The range keeps every requested ray: rejected and missing rays remain unresolved. It is a missingness range, not a confidence interval or resemblance probability. Each side records its first failed rule. Weak, ambiguous or out-of-window edges cannot establish agreement. These gradients may describe texture rather than anatomical boundaries; tangential motion is not measured.

Registered views

Interactive opacity inspection

Changes only the display; it does not re-estimate landmarks or recompute any metric.

Read the units before the number.
Landmark residuals are normalized by the geometric mean of registered interocular spans. A within-tolerance fraction counts landmarks below the declared threshold (0.05 spans). Neither quantity is an identity probability. The intervals below measure conditional observation sensitivity, not established detector accuracy.

Shape relations without a frozen alignment.

Eight reference landmarks per source. Each relationship keeps its own geometry and unit. The error sets propagate through the uncertain reference eye span; moving the display or fitting the pair cannot erase that uncertainty.

What this range does—and does not—establish

All bounds describe reference positions within the supplied eight-point error sets. No coordinates are corrected and no error model is fitted here. A lower bound above tolerance establishes separation under those sets; an upper bound below tolerance establishes agreement under them. An unavailable or unresolved relation is not counted as agreement. A matched-relation fraction is not facial resemblance probability.

Distances, unsigned angles and bilateral contrasts are reflection-insensitive. Oriented areas and the proper-rotation shape distance retain reflection sensitivity under fixed point correspondence. The finite directional calculations use conservative corrections and float64 padding; they are not exact extrema or formally verified interval arithmetic.

Statistical coverage transfers only under the original source-calibration assumptions. A new acquisition domain or a poorly generalized detector is not repaired by these geometric bounds.

WAVE 07 / CORRELATED REFERENCE ERROR

One error field. Eight connected landmarks.

A shared localization shift should not become eight unrelated anatomical changes. This inspector displays the frozen full-shape error set and its marginal-product relaxation. It does not move the observations or update any measurement.

Shared full16 set · proper-rotation shape RMSJoint dependencies retained through normalization and refitting.
Same set → product of marginal ellipsesSame centers, marginal blocks and q. This discards dependence; it is not a separately fitted baseline.

Coherent displacement mode

One shared latent coefficient moves all points together. The solid outline is the set center; displaced markers are a selected admissible error, not a new prediction. Eigenmode signs are conventional; tied eigenbases are not unique physical mechanisms.

Full coordinate correlation

Select a cell to inspect its exact covariance and correlation.

Coordinate order is point 0 x,y through point 7 x,y. Teal is positive, amber is negative. Correlation describes the fitted error model—not similarity between people or confidence in a match.

Raw arraysDevelopment fit + calibrationFull relation inventory

The plotted matrix is the development-derived error covariance transported into this source chart. The original perturbation covariance remains separately exported. Narrower algebraic bounds do not repair dataset shift or establish human detector accuracy.

Image-edge support

Landmark-guided normal-ray searches. Matching image gradients are diagnostic, not proof of correct anatomy. Landmarks are never moved to an edge candidate. Complete ray responses and rejection masks are in arrays.npz.

Locate the measured image edges

Only rays localized in both images are drawn. Unresolved rays remain in the table denominator. These markers show selected gradients, not corrected anatomical landmarks.

Reference-calibrated localization envelope

Development-qualified error centers. The observed gap remains the raw measurement. The bounds use reference-position centers shifted by the frozen development-only localization-bias model. The mesh, raster, registration and measured geometry have not moved. A raw gap need not lie inside an interval for the independently referenced gap.

Scope: calibration_reference_domain. Acquisition domain: Frozen HELEN roots [132,192), new correspondence-v2 joint fit; published PTS agreement; anatomical equivalence and visibility unresolved. These bounds hold the observed transforms and normalization fixed; they are not confidence intervals for re-fitted true shape or identity.
